in zebrafis, the earliest CD41-GFP(low) HCSs emerge in the AGM and enter the circulation through the axial vein.

the developmental migration of CD41+ HSCs in zebrafis.
the developmental origin of HSCs and their migration to the thymus.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zebrafish HSCs emerge from the AGM and seed the caudally located hematopoietic tissues, including the thymus, through an intravascular and extravascular migration.

zebrafish HSCs are not intrinsically different from mammalian HSCs but that they follow a distinct developmental route that has been obscured by the lack of suitable tools to visualize their emergence.
in zebrafis, HSCs emerge from the subaortic region, enter the circulation through the axial vein and seed the caudally localized hematopoietic tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in zebrafis, HSCs are born in the AGM as CD41-GFP(high) precursors, and then travel to the caudal hematoietic tissue and the thymus, where they undergo a further maturation process.
the AGM is the first site of HSC emergence in the zebrafis, and that emerging HSCs migrate through the axial vein to the caudal hemopoetic tissue and thymus.
the zebrafish model allows us for the first-time to image the behavior of emerging HSCs and their early colonization of the thymus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zebrafish HSCs emerge from the AGM and seed hematopoietic and lymphoid organs in a manner that is strikingly similar to mammalian HSCs.

the zebrafish embryo is a unique model to image HSC emergence and migration in real time, allowing us to visualize and quantify the dynamics of the HSC niche and the behavior of HSC precursors in the AGM and in the first hematopoietic organ.
zebrafish is an excellent system to study HSC emergence, migration, and colonization in a live animal.
